series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: Fetch last FETCH=365 daily highs and lows; compute per-bar mid=(high+low)/2 then mid.Mean() as year-to-date volatility midpoint. Close above midpoint → bullish price_state=+1; below → −1. Require price_state to agree with engulfing candle state before any trade.
data_needed: 365 D1 high/low bars; current close; engulfing open/close of bars 0 and 1.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY PERIOD_D1; ATR(14) for stops; backtest 2020-01-01 to 2024-11
why_new_for_mis: Turns rolling YTD high–low midpoint into an explicit elevated-vs-depressed price/volatility context sensor that gates pattern signals—portable beyond candlestick EAs.
quote: we will calculate the midpoint formed by the last year to date of historical high and low prices offered in the market... restrict our application to only place long positions when the Close price is above the historical high-low midpoint

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: Two EMAs on PRICE_HIGH and PRICE_LOW (period 90) form a non-crossing channel. Full candle outside the channel = imbalance: open&close above ma_high → long; open&close below ma_low → short. Exit when price re-enters the channel.
data_needed: EMA(high) and EMA(low) buffers; open/close of current bar.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY D1; MA_PERIOD=90; confluence with engulfing + YTD midpoint
why_new_for_mis: Defines a stable-vs-imbalanced regime from dual high/low MAs without requiring crossover—MIS can treat outside-channel closes as imbalance onset.
quote: price levels between the high and low moving average are considered stable. Whereas, when price levels form beyond the region between the 2 moving averages, we perceive an imbalance in the market.

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: On higher TF (D1), take mean of last bars_used of MA(20); range_zone_ub/lb = mid ± atr_multiple×ATR(14). Map close into zones: 1 (above ub)=bull trend, 2 (mid..ub)=mean-revert sell, 3 (lb..mid)=mean-revert buy, 4 (below lb)=bear trend. Same MA(100) event (close>MA) is followed in zones 1/4 and reversed in 2/3.
data_needed: D1 MA(20) buffer mean over bars_used; D1 ATR(14); trading-TF MA(100); atr_multiple input.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1 trade TF with D1 channel; backtest ~2020-01-01 to 2025-01-06; atr_multiple≈1–2, bars_used=30
why_new_for_mis: Frames markets as continuously alternating trend/range zones via an ATR-scaled MA channel rather than a binary classifier—direct regime and regime-change sensor.
quote: Trend Mode: The market can only truly trend in either Zone 1 or Zone 4. Range Mode: The market can only truly be range bound in Zone 2 or Zone 3.

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: Gradient-descent logistic on Δopen/Δhigh/Δlow/Δclose over look_ahead bars; labels future close fall=1 (default/sell). Cutoff is not 0.5 but baseline=(max_forecast+min_forecast)/2 of in-sample sigmoid outputs. If BB breach + stochastic confirm and (prediction−baseline) aligns with side, scale lot ×2 (and add extra lots).
data_needed: fetch bars of OHLC; look_ahead horizon; ATR; Bollinger; Stochastic; learning_rate.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD PERIOD_M15; BB period 90 SD 2; 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-30
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a probability-of-continuation sensor with a market-calibrated dynamic cutoff, usable as confidence for sizing or gating without fixed 0.5.
quote: I included an additional step to calculate an optimal cut-off point by first recording the maximum and minimum odds forecasted by our model. We then bisected the true range of predictions given by our model to find our cut-off point.

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: Copy BARS≈half available M15 RSI readings; rsi_midpoint=(Max+Min)/2 of observed range (not fixed 50); rsi_growth=|rsi−mid|; enter only if (rsi−mid) exceeds ±(Mean(rsi_growth)×BIG_SIZE) with BIG_SIZE=2, on S/R breakouts from D1 high/low 5 bars ago.
data_needed: RSI buffer over BARS; ATR for SL; D1 support/resistance lookback SUPPORT_PERIOD=5.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAGUSD; TF_1=D1 levels, TF_2=M15 RSI(10); backtest 2017-01-01 to 2025-01-28
why_new_for_mis: Replaces fixed 30/70 with market-specific RSI mid and 2× average deviation—cross-symbol comparable strength sensor when classical levels never fire.
quote: we will bisect the 2 parallel lines that mark the maximum and minimum output generated by the indicator. This bisecting line becomes our new midpoint... only enter its positions, if it observes a change in the RSI value 2 times greater than an average move

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: MLPRegressor (5,10,4,2) trained on z-scored OHLC+MA14 to forecast MA14 LOOK_AHEAD=48 M30 bars ahead; ONNX in EA. Enter only if forecast MA continues with trade and forecast MA stays on profitable side of fixed SL; while open, if forecast MA threatensens SL, relocate SL to forecast (or tighten if forecast < open).
data_needed: M30 OHLC + MA14 series; train mean/std; ONNX model; yesterday high/low from D1.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; TF_1=D1 levels, TF_2=M30; backtest 2022-01-01 to 2025-01-01; LOOK_AHEAD=48 (~1 day)
why_new_for_mis: Uses easier-to-forecast MA path as a stop-hit risk sensor—MIS can gate or resize exposure when predicted indicator path intersects stop/risk levels.
quote: forecasting if the future value of the moving average, is expected to surpass our stop loss level. If our computer expects that to be the case, then it should not place any trades

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: Export 14 RSI periods (5..70 step 5) plus HORIZON=10 differences; Ridge on Diff RSI features with α/tol grid; largest |coef| picks period (Diff RSI 55). Second grid on change thresholds finds optimal ~9 RSI levels (±0.5σ bands 7.17–10.82). RandomForestRegressor on Diff RSI 55 → P(bull)>0.5 supplies missing long signals.
data_needed: Grid of RSI handlers; 10-day returns; train excluding backtest window; ONNX RF optional.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_D1; RSI 55; backtest 2022-01-01 to 2025-03; train ends before backtest
why_new_for_mis: Automates indicator-period and threshold selection via coefficient importance and threshold RMSE search—MIS can retune oscillator sensors per symbol without manual 30/70.
quote: it was the 10-period change in the 55 period RSI that obtained the largest coefficients from our best performing model.

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: Stack OHLC, HORIZON diffs, 14 WPR levels (5..70) and their diffs (36 cols); UMAP(n_components=2, n_neighbors=30) yields embeddings that beat raw features vs TSS baseline. MLP learns UMAP map then second MLP forecasts 10-day return from 2 embeddings; ONNX pair in EA. Lot×2 when embedding forecast disagrees with open/close mean reversal cue.
data_needed: 14 WPR buffers + OHLC/diffs; train Z1/Z2; UMAP+embedded ONNX models.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURGBP PERIOD_D1; train ~2002-11 to 2018-08; test from 2023; HORIZON=10
why_new_for_mis: Compresses many indicator periods into a low-dim nonlinear state usable as a regime/feature sensor—avoids picking one WPR period.
quote: using 2 embedded UMAP components, we outperformed an equivalent model using all the market data in its original form

series_key: build self optimizing expert advisors in mql5
mechanism: Identical-period MAs on PRICE_CLOSE vs PRICE_OPEN: close-MA > open-MA ⇒ bullish (avg close above avg open); reverse ⇒ bearish. Virtual Strategy.BuySignal/SellSignal; walk-forward genetic search on period/holding/TF validates forward Sharpe stability.
data_needed: Two MA handlers (open & close applied price); holding period; optional genetic inputs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Daily TF default MA_PERIOD=10 HOLDING_PERIOD=5; forward 1/2 genetic Sharpe optimize
why_new_for_mis: Open-vs-close MA gap is a compact bullish/bearish sentiment regime feature distinct from classic dual-period crossovers.
quote: if the average Close price is greater than the average Open price, then price action can be seen as bullish, and a strong trend in the direction may persist.

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
mechanism: Constraint: only buy if prior D1 close>open (bullish day), only sell if D1 close<open. On that filter, Donchian upper/lower breakout (close > ExtUpBuffer / < ExtDnBuffer) fires entries. Separate RSI+EMA50/200 trend-following path runs in parallel under same D1 constraint philosophy.
data_needed: Donchian Channel iCustom buffers 0/2; D1 open/close bar 1; optional RSI and EMA50/200.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Volatility 150 (1s) Index demo; Donchian period 20; chart TF of EA + PERIOD_D1 sentiment
why_new_for_mis: Uses higher-TF candle body sign as a hard regime gate on lower-TF channel breakouts—simple multi-TF sentiment sensor for MIS.
quote: we only buy when there is a bullish D1 candlestick, and we sell when there is a bearish D1 candlestick... Buy condition: Closing price is above the upper Donchian band on a bullish day

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
mechanism: Compare price extremes at bars 2 vs DivergenceLookBack against MACD buffer extremes: regular bullish = lower price low + higher MACD low; regular bearish = higher price high + lower MACD high; hidden bullish/bearish invert for continuation. Confirm with MACD vs signal line; allow trades only when D1 candle is bullish (buys) or bearish (sells).
data_needed: MACD main+signal buffers over lookback; iHigh/iLow at 2 and lookback; D1 open/close.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M15 tester; Boom 300 Index H4 divergence illustrations; DivergenceLookBack=8
why_new_for_mis: Encodes regular vs hidden divergence as distinct reversal-vs-continuation change sensors aligned to daily regime.
quote: Regular divergence signals potential trend reversals... Hidden divergence, on the other hand, suggests trend continuation.

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
mechanism: Fast EMA(50) vs slow EMA(200): Golden Cross (fast crosses above slow) → buy; Death Cross (fast crosses below) → sell. Intentionally NOT gated by D1 sentiment so it can catch reversals while other Trend Constraint modules stay constrained; exit when MAs re-cross against the position.
data_needed: Fast/slow EMA handles; 2-bar buffers for cross detection.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Boom 500 Index M5 tester; FastEMAPeriod=50 SlowEMAPeriod=200; merged as UseGoldenDeathCrossStrategy module
why_new_for_mis: Treats classic MA cross as an independent reversal-change channel that can fire against the higher-TF candle regime—useful as a dedicated break-of-regime sensor.
quote: Unlike constrained strategies that depend on daily market sentiment, these crossover strategies operate independently to identify and act on reversals as they occur.

mechanism: Replace fixed-point SL/TP with stopDistance=ATR(ATRPeriod)×ATRMultiplier and TP=stopDistance×TPRatio at entry (using live ATR[0]). Before any order, IsSpreadAcceptable(): (ask−bid)/_Point must be ≤ MaxSpreadPips×10, else skip—spread acts as live liquidity/friction gate.
data_needed: ATR handle; SymbolInfoTick ask/bid; MaxSpreadPips; ATRMultiplier; TPRatio.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MA crossover EA on chart symbol/period; ATRPeriod=14 ATRMultiplier=1.5 TPRatio=2.0; MaxSpreadPips=2.0 example
why_new_for_mis: Packages ATR distance and live spread cap as volatility and liquidity sensors that gate execution—portable beyond this MA tutorial.
quote: By basing stop-loss and take-profit calculations on ATR, the EA automatically adapts its risk parameters to current market conditions... verify that the current spread remains below a user-defined threshold.
